title: Scan Several Paper Pages Into One PDF on iPhone
description: Scan several paper pages into one PDF on iPhone. Keep the scan open for all sheets and check the saved file before you attach it.
direct: Keep the scan session open until the last sheet, save one PDF, and reopen that exact file to confirm the page count.
figureAlt: Top-down realistic document scanning with three distinct sheets in reading order, a phone hovering over the first sheet and a hand positioning the page
cards.decision.heading: Count the pages before scanning
cards.decision.body: Put the sheets in reading order. Count the reverse side too if it has information. Keep the finished pages in a separate pile so you can see which sheets are left.
sections.detail-1.heading: Check the copy you send
sections.detail-1.body: Open the attachment preview before sending. If it shows a count, compare it to the PDF you checked in Files. If there is a size limit, compress a copy and make sure the smallest text still reads.
sections.detail-2.heading: About the app
sections.detail-2.body: Space Sheep Studio develops this iPhone app. Check the App Store listing for current access and export options.
faqs.first-question.heading: Can I include both sides of one sheet?
faqs.first-question.body: Yes. Scan each side as a separate page in the same session.
faqs.second-question.heading: What exactly should I attach?
faqs.second-question.body: Attach the saved PDF from Files. A shared preview could contain only the visible page.

steps.step-1.text: Use the scan tool in PDF Compressor: Sign & Merge. Check the edges of the first capture.
steps.step-2.text: Add the other pages before finishing the scan. If you already saved separate PDFs, merge them in the right order.
steps.step-3.text: Save the PDF to Files. Reopen that exact file, confirm the count and check the first, last and any retaken pages.
